items.text: System and/or component effectivity for a particular aircraft version/cockpit and engine version is denoted by a letter code enclosed in a box located in the text or on an illustration.
An asterisk (*) preceding steps is used to highlight procedures for D aircraft which apply to both DF Front and DR Rear cockpits.
The following definitions apply to Warnings, Cautions, Notes, and Comms found throughout the manual:
Operating procedures, techniques, etc., which could result in personal injury or loss of life if not carefully followed.
Operating procedures, techniques, etc., which could result in damage to equipment if not carefully followed.
An operating procedure, technique, etc., which is considered essential to emphasize with additional information.
EPU CHECK (boxed warning heading): Aircraft system, component, procedure, that special attention, techniques, etc., is required.
Use of words As Desired and As Required
As desired allows pilot preference in switch/control positioning.
As required indicates those actions which vary based on mission requirements or dedicated SOP instructions.

This section is furnished for familiarization use. It will normally be inserted between BEFORE ENTERING COCKPIT and COCKPIT INTERIOR CHECK. It may also be inserted in another part of the checklist, removed, parts removed, or discarded as desired.

A thorough cockpit interior preflight shall be accomplished prior to each flight. The design features of the aircraft greatly simplify this task, but do not alleviate the requirement. Switch positions designated AS DESIRED allow pilot preference in switch/control positioning. AS REQUIRED indicates those switches that will differ with mission requirements. If no specific requirement exists, pilot preference may be used. Normally, those avionics switches designated AS DESIRED or AS REQUIRED should be OFF for start.

items.action: OFF (CC, AAI, IFF, RADAR, ILS/TACAN, VSD, HUD, INS, TEWS)

items.text: Normal engine start procedure does not use external power. With the JFS running, power is available to operate the AMAD fire warning system, the intercom system between pilot and the ground, and the cockpit utility light. Engine RPM and FTIT gages are inoperative until the emergency generator comes on line during start. The rest of the engine instruments are inoperative until a main generator comes on line at about 44% RPM during the first engine start.

(PW-220) ENG CONTR switch position should not be changed until 60 seconds after start initiation due to the possible failure of the CGB shear section, hot start, start-stall, or torching during start. Switch may be positioned to desired setting once engine achieves idle.

Because a JFS accumulator was discharged to start the JFS, the JFS LOW light will illuminate when power is available to light the caution panel. It will go out when the accumulators are recharged by a running engine.

When the finger lift is raised, the JFS will engage and accelerate the engine. JFS engagement is indicated by an audible decrease in JFS whine when the JFS clutch engages (BMS sounds WIP). A normal start is indicated by RPM acceleration occurring before initial FTIT movement.

Monitor engine instruments and compare against the operating limitations listed in section V. After first engine start, the JFS automatically decouples from that engine and is ready for the second engine start. After second engine start, the JFS shuts down automatically.

If an engine must be shut down and restarted before the JFS low light has extinguished, avoid starting the JFS on a partially charged bottle. Service the JFS via the ground comm menu (T, 7) prior to a second JFS start attempt.
The following procedure is applicable to either engine. The right engine is normally started first to permit checking utility hydraulic pressure with only the right pump operating.

items.note: Observe the AMAD fire warning light on and voice warning activated.
This engages the JFS to the engine.
Check AMAD, left and right ENG FIRE lights ON, and voice warning activated.

Monitor FTIT for hot start.
Monitor oil pressure rises into green arc.
Check AB BURN THRU lights ON and voice warning activated, (main generator must be on line). The AMAD and ENG FIRE lights will also be activated.

Finger lift – RAISE AND RELEASE
Other throttle – IDLE 25%
Other engine instruments – CHECK

items.action: CONFIRM OFF; start light out JFS SWITCH remains ON

items.text:
INS alignment is initiated.
After 60sec - End Coarse - solid ALN light
After 120sec - End partial - 1Hz flash ALN light
After 240sec - full align - 4Hz flash ALN light

items.note: Wait for "TERMINAL LOAD: INITIALIZE" to display.
The CC buffer must be cleared to ensure data from the previous flight does not contaminate data for this flight (WIP)

items.text: F-15C trim system is WIP – trim inputs on ground will give no feedback until airborne. Extreme care should be taken not to make inadvertent trim inputs while on ground.
Stick full aft and full left
items.action: Observe stabilator trailing edge up (left further up than the right) rudders 30° left, left aileron up, right aileron down

items.text: Stick full forward and full left
items.action: Observer right stabilator leading edge moves into view and rudders move 30° right (ailerons should not move)

items.text: Stick full forward and full right
items.action: Observe left aileron moves down and right aileron moves up, rudders move 30° left, and left stabilator leading edge in view

items.text: Stick full aft and full right
items.action: Observe stabilator trailing edge moves to full up (right higher than left) and rudders move 30° right (ailerons do not move)
Check. Hold stick neutral and paddle switch pressed. Move rudder pedals left and right and observe 15° rudder travel (CAS off)

items.text: Failure to ensure all flight control surfaces move to the proper position for each stick movement may result in loss of control. Malfunctions can exist which would cause the flight controls to be correct with stick in one position and incorrect in another position.

Release brakes and advance power slightly if necessary. As aircraft starts to roll, apply brakes to check operation. When clear, actuate nose gear steering in both directions to ensure proper operation. During taxi, check all flight instruments. Due to excess thrust at idle power, taxi speed requires continual attention. At high gross weights, make all turns at minimum practicable speed and maximum practicable radius.

items.note: If the aircraft is manually trimmed nose down from takeoff trim, nosewheel lift-off speed may be increased.
The canopy may bounce slightly as it lowers on canopy sill.

items.text: Advance engines to 80% (some aircraft creep may occur) and check instruments. When ready for takeoff, release brakes and advance throttles to MIL or MAX as desired.
Monitor engine instruments for proper operation, assuring that nozzles remain below 30% at MIL.

For normal takeoffs, move the stick to approximately 10° pitch attitude. For maximum performance takeoffs (minimum ground roll), move the stick full aft at a speed below the nose wheel lift-off speed and rotate 12° pitch attitude.
Retract gear and flaps when airborne.

During normal afterburner operation, observe exhaust nozzles open progressively with each afterburner segment; thrust and fuel flow increase proportionately. As throttles are advanced from minimum to maximum afterburner, the increase in thrust is fairly smooth and continuous.
MIL Power - Climb at 350 knots to 0.90 Mach, then maintain 0.90 MACH.
MAX Power - Climb at 350 knots to 0,95 Mach. If Mach increases above 0,95 at 40° pitch attitude, hold 40° and allow the Mach to increase.
Continually monitor aircraft systems operation throughout the flight. Frequently check engine instruments, cabin pressure, oxygen system operation, fuel quantity and fuel transfer.

Optimal cruise and maximum endurance should be found in the performance data section and is attained by flying the correct Mach number for configuration and altitude. If the performance charts are not available and accuracy is not a significant factor, 12 units AOA may be used for optimum cruise and 14.5 units AOA may be used for maximum endurance.

items.action: OFF (AAI, IFF, ILS/TACAN, VSD, MPCD, HUD, INS(NCI), and TEWS)
items.note: Turn avionics OFF before engine shutdown to prevent false BIT warnings on the status panel (N/I)

items.text: Prior to engine shutdown, advance throttle(s) to 75-78% for 5-10 seconds (local safety conditions permitting)
Retard throttle(s) to IDLE, stabilize minimum of 1-2 seconds

items.note: Wait 10 seconds after INS shutoff before placing throttle(s) off. After the last generator is off and before the emergency generator drops off line, ensure that the L and R GEN OUT lights and the landing gear indicator lights come on. Illumination of these lights indicates that the generator failure circuit is functioning and the emergency generator is supplying both AC and DC essential power.

items.text: Complete your Before Flight procedures through Before Taxiing
Check aircraft for loose doors and fasteners, cracks, dents, leaks, and other discrepancies.
See chart in document, page N-14 (Figure N-3, Exterior Inspection).
See chart in document, page N-17 (Figure N-4, Servicing Diagram).

Blank TOLD card form (Conditions: GW, Runway Condition, Runway Temp, Pressure Altitude, Wind, Runway Length, Runway Slope for Takeoff/Landing; Takeoff: Rotation Speed, Takeoff Speed/Dist., Refusal Speed, Max Brake Speed; Landing: Approach Speed, Touchdown Speed, Landing Distance for Immediately After Takeoff and Final Landing GW). See chart in document, page N-18 (Figure N-5).
1. BMS F-15 PW220 ENGINE MODEL IS WIP AND USES START LIMITS FROM THE REAL AIRCRAFT.
3. IN PHASE FLUCTUATION OF MORE THEN ONE INSTRUMENT, OR SHORT TERM CYCLIC FLUCTUATIONS ACCOMPANIED BY THRUST SURGES, INDICATE ENGINE ENTROL PROBLEMS.
4. NOZZLE FLUCTUATIONS ARE LIMIED TO +- 2% AT MILITARY POWER AND ABOVE. FLUCTUATIONS ARE NOT PERMITTED BELOW MILITARY POWER.
5. FOR ENGINE OPERATION AT MILITARY OR ABOVE, OIL PRESSURE MUST INCREASE 15 PSI MINIMUM ABOVE IDLE OIL PRESSURE.
6. ENGINE NOZZLE POSITION IS LIMITED TO 30% OPEN OR LESS AT MILITARY POWER.

BMS’s F-15C caution panel is work in progress: its lights currently all show red (the caution lights should be yellow), and not all of them work (Dash-1 3.23.1). The warning and caution light test is WIP and the LT TEST switch is not implemented; the fire warning system is not yet simulated.

items.title: L BURN THRU
items.text: Left burn-through light on the fire warning panel: the Dash-1 lists it as the fire detection loop burn-through indication, and the checklist calls these the AB BURN THRU lights. BMS does not yet simulate the fire warning and extinguishing system.
items.action: No fire procedure in the BMS F-15C checklist. In the engine start fire test (step 16) it must come on with the voice warning once a main generator is on line.

items.title: R BURN THRU
items.text: Right burn-through light on the fire warning panel: the Dash-1 lists it as the fire detection loop burn-through indication, and the checklist calls these the AB BURN THRU lights. BMS does not yet simulate the fire warning and extinguishing system.
items.action: No fire procedure in the BMS F-15C checklist. In the engine start fire test (step 16) it must come on with the voice warning once a main generator is on line.

items.title: AMAD FIRE PUSH
items.text: Airframe-mounted accessory drive (AMAD) fire/overheat light on the fire warning panel. BMS does not yet simulate the fire warning and extinguishing system.
items.action: No fire procedure in the BMS F-15C checklist. The AMAD fire warning works as soon as the JFS runs: the start fire tests (steps 5, 9 and 16) must light it with the voice warning.

items.title: ENG FIRE PUSH (L)
items.text: Left engine bay fire/overheat light (the lamp reads ENG FIRE PUSH, with an arrow pointing left). BMS does not yet simulate the fire warning and extinguishing system.
items.action: No fire procedure in the BMS F-15C checklist. Per the Dash-1, pushing the light shuts off bleed air and fuel to that engine and arms its extinguisher; DISCHARGE/TEST to DISCHARGE fires it. The start fire test (step 9) must light it.

items.title: ENG FIRE PUSH (R)
items.text: Right engine bay fire/overheat light (the lamp reads ENG FIRE PUSH, with an arrow pointing right). BMS does not yet simulate the fire warning and extinguishing system.
items.action: No fire procedure in the BMS F-15C checklist. Per the Dash-1, pushing the light shuts off bleed air and fuel to that engine and arms its extinguisher; DISCHARGE/TEST to DISCHARGE fires it. The start fire test (step 9) must light it.

items.title: CANOPY UNLOCKED
items.action: Canopy – CLOSED AND LOCKED before takeoff (Before Takeoff, step 7). Airborne, the Training Manual says it means you took off with the canopy open: close it before the next takeoff.

items.title: GEAR HANDLE
items.text: Red light in the landing gear handle: on while the gear is in transit. If it stays on, a gear malfunction is indicated.
items.action: Stay below 300 kt. Gear handle DOWN; if the gear shows down, land as soon as possible. If not, below 190 kt pull the EMERG LG handle and check three greens with the handle light out (no nosewheel steering afterwards).

items.title: MASTER CAUTION
items.text: Comes on with any caution light except AV BIT, JFS LOW, SPD BK OUT and the spare.
items.action: Press it to reset (MASTER CAUTION switch on the main communications panel). The caution light stays on until the fault is corrected, except HYDRAULIC and AUTO PLT, which go out with it.

items.title: SPD BK OUT
items.text: The speed brake is extended or partly extended (above 25 units AOA it retracts by itself). It does not bring on MASTER CAUTION.
items.action: Retract the speed brake if you do not want it. Before taxi, cycle the speed brake and check the light goes out (step 10).

items.title: RUDR LMTR
items.text: Shown on BMS’s caution panel, but no BMS F-15C manual says what lights it.
items.action: No procedure in the BMS F-15C checklist.

items.title: BST SYS MAL
items.text: The emergency fuel boost pump is running on an abnormal power source. During start it comes on about 30 s after the first main generator, when the emergency generator drops off line, and goes out when the second main generator comes on line.
items.action: Normal during engine start: it must go out once both generators are on line. No in-flight procedure in the BMS F-15C checklist.

items.title: FUEL HOT
items.text: Shown on BMS’s caution panel, but no BMS F-15C manual says what lights it.
items.action: No procedure in the BMS F-15C checklist.

items.title: TOT TEMP HI
items.text: Shown on BMS’s caution panel, but no BMS F-15C manual says what lights it.
items.action: No procedure in the BMS F-15C checklist.

items.title: ATTITUDE
items.text: Shown on BMS’s caution panel, but no BMS F-15C manual says what lights it.
items.action: No procedure in the BMS F-15C checklist.

items.title: L BST PMP
items.text: Left main boost pump (it alone feeds the left engine). The Dash-1 does not describe the light; it says that if a main boost pump fails the emergency boost pump comes on and the remaining pumps feed both engines.
items.action: No procedure in the BMS F-15C checklist. The Dash-1 warns that a boost pump failure limits afterburner use, and that losing both main pumps and the emergency pump can flame out both engines.

items.title: R BST PMP
items.text: Right main boost pump (it alone feeds the right engine). The Dash-1 does not describe the light; it says that if a main boost pump fails the emergency boost pump comes on and the remaining pumps feed both engines.
items.action: No procedure in the BMS F-15C checklist. The Dash-1 warns that a boost pump failure limits afterburner use, and that losing both main pumps and the emergency pump can flame out both engines.

items.title: L INLET
items.text: Shown on BMS’s caution panel, but no BMS F-15C manual says what lights it.
items.action: No procedure in the BMS F-15C checklist.

items.title: R INLET
items.text: Shown on BMS’s caution panel, but no BMS F-15C manual says what lights it.
items.action: No procedure in the BMS F-15C checklist.

items.title: IFF MODE 4
items.text: The Dash-1 says only that the caution panel has an IFF mode 4 light; it does not say what lights it.
items.action: No procedure in the BMS F-15C checklist.

items.title: AV BIT
items.text: Avionics BIT light. It does not bring on MASTER CAUTION, and BMS does not implement the F-15C’s built-in test system.
items.action: No procedure in the BMS F-15C checklist.

items.title: JFS LOW
items.text: The JFS start discharged an accumulator: the light comes on once the caution panel has power and goes out when a running engine has recharged the accumulators. It does not bring on MASTER CAUTION.
items.action: Must be out before taxi (step 19). While it is on, emergency brakes and steering are not reliable for taxi, and a second JFS start should wait until the JFS is serviced (ground comm menu T, 7).
items.note: Checklist pages N-5, N-8, EP-5 · Dash-1 pages 25, 54

items.title: L GEN OUT
items.text: The left generator is off line: it took itself off after a fault, or its GEN switch is OFF. The right generator then powers every bus (the ECM pod is not simulated) and the emergency generator comes on.
items.action: Once the fault has cleared, cycle that GEN switch (engine control panel) to bring it back; after an underfrequency trip it returns by itself. At engine shutdown both GEN OUT lights must come on (checklist N-12).

items.title: R GEN OUT
items.text: The right generator is off line: it took itself off after a fault, or its GEN switch is OFF. The left generator then powers every bus (the ECM pod is not simulated) and the emergency generator comes on.
items.action: Once the fault has cleared, cycle that GEN switch (engine control panel) to bring it back; after an underfrequency trip it returns by itself. At engine shutdown both GEN OUT lights must come on (checklist N-12).

items.title: EMER BST ON
items.text: The emergency fuel boost pump is running: it runs after a main boost pump, main generator or double transformer-rectifier failure, and during start until both main generators are on line.
items.action: During start: check it ON after the first engine (step 14) and out once both generators are on line. No in-flight procedure in the BMS F-15C checklist.

items.title: HYDRAULIC
items.text: Comes on with any hydraulic caution on the BIT panel (not simulated): a circuit shut off by the reservoir level sensing system after a leak, or low utility pump pressure.
items.action: Read the hydraulic pressure indicators. Resetting MASTER CAUTION also puts this light out. Losing UTL A takes the normal brakes: see Loss of Brakes.

items.title: OIL PRESS
items.action: On start, if oil pressure does not rise into the green arc, throttle OFF at once. Limits: 15–80 psi at idle, 30–80 psi at MIL/AB. No in-flight procedure in the BMS F-15C checklist.
items.note: Dash-1 pages 11, 58 · checklist pages N-5, N-19

items.title: INLET ICE
items.text: Ice is building up in the engine inlet (inlet ice detector). Not simulated in BMS: the Dash-1 marks this light N/I.
items.action: Engine anti-ice with the ENG HEAT switch (ECS panel) and leave the icing. The DEEC turns engine anti-ice off above 30,000 ft or 15°C inlet temperature.

items.title: PITCH RATIO
items.text: The Dash-1 does not describe the light. It says the pitch ratio drives to an intermediate position and locks if hydraulic pressure is lost, and that the pitch ratio switch and indicator do not work in BMS.
items.action: No procedure in the BMS F-15C checklist.

items.title: ROLL RATIO
items.text: The Dash-1 does not describe the light. It says the roll ratio drives to mid-range and locks if UTL A and PC2A hydraulic pressure are lost or the roll ratio switch is in EMER (not simulated), and the aileron-rudder interconnect then stops working.
items.action: No procedure in the BMS F-15C checklist.

items.title: ANTI SKID
items.text: The anti-skid system has failed (it is only checked when the gear comes down), or the anti-skid switch is in PULSER. A failure can leave the aileron-rudder interconnect engaged after touchdown.
items.action: If the brakes fail: anti-skid switch PULSER at high speed or OFF at taxi speed; if braking does not return, pull the emergency brake/steer handle. OFF or PULSER also frees the ARI.
items.note: Dash-1 pages 18, 21, 42 · checklist pages EP-5, EP-6

items.title: L EEC
items.text: The left engine’s DEEC is in its secondary mode (the Dash-1 calls this the ENG CONTR light), after a DEEC fault or with the EEC switch OFF: no afterburner, RPM held to about 80%, nozzle almost closed.
items.action: It stays in this mode until the fault clears and the engine’s EEC (ENG CONTR) switch is cycled. On takeoff, treat it as an afterburner failure/loss of thrust. Before taxi, cycling the switches must bring the lights on and out (step 17).

items.title: R EEC
items.text: The right engine’s DEEC is in its secondary mode (the Dash-1 calls this the ENG CONTR light), after a DEEC fault or with the EEC switch OFF: no afterburner, RPM held to about 80%, nozzle almost closed.
items.action: It stays in this mode until the fault clears and the engine’s EEC (ENG CONTR) switch is cycled. On takeoff, treat it as an afterburner failure/loss of thrust. Before taxi, cycling the switches must bring the lights on and out (step 17).

items.title: CAS YAW
items.text: The yaw CAS axis has failed or is disengaged (the dual-channel CAS turns an axis off when it fails). A moderate yaw transient when yaw CAS drops out or re-engages is normal.
items.action: Check the YAW CAS switch is ON (CAS panel); the checklist’s CAS reset is not implemented in BMS. The autopilot needs all three CAS axes.

items.title: CAS ROLL
items.text: The roll CAS axis has failed or is disengaged (the dual-channel CAS turns an axis off when it fails). CAS moves the stabilators and rudders only, not the ailerons.
items.action: Check the ROLL CAS switch is ON (CAS panel); the checklist’s CAS reset is not implemented in BMS. The autopilot needs all three CAS axes.

items.title: CAS PITCH
items.text: The pitch CAS axis has failed or is disengaged (the dual-channel CAS turns an axis off when it fails). The hydromechanical controls alone can still fly the aircraft.
items.action: Check the PITCH CAS switch is ON (CAS panel); the checklist’s CAS reset is not implemented in BMS. The autopilot needs all three CAS axes.

items.title: L BLEED AIR
items.text: Shown on BMS’s caution panel, but no BMS F-15C manual says what lights it. Engine bleed air feeds the ECS and is selected with the AIR SOURCE knob.
items.action: No procedure in the BMS F-15C checklist.

items.title: R BLEED AIR
items.text: Shown on BMS’s caution panel, but no BMS F-15C manual says what lights it. Engine bleed air feeds the ECS and is selected with the AIR SOURCE knob.
items.action: No procedure in the BMS F-15C checklist.

items.title: WNDSHLD HOT
items.text: Shown on BMS’s caution panel, but no BMS F-15C manual says what lights it. The ECS supplies windshield anti-fog and anti-ice.
items.action: No procedure in the BMS F-15C checklist.

items.title: FUEL LOW
items.text: Engine feed tank fuel is low; the Dash-1 mentions this light only in passing and gives no quantity.
items.action: No procedure in the BMS F-15C checklist. With one engine shut down, its feed tank is only drawn on once the running engine’s feed tank is well below the FUEL LOW level.

items.title: BINGO FUEL
items.text: Shown on BMS’s caution panel; the Dash-1 does not describe the light, and its glossary defines BINGO as the return fuel state.
items.action: No procedure in the BMS F-15C checklist.

items.title: OXY LOW
items.text: Shown on BMS’s caution panel, but no BMS F-15C manual says what lights it. The Training Manual says oxygen quantity is not modelled yet.
items.action: No procedure in the BMS F-15C checklist. Before taxi: oxygen quantity CHECK, supply ON (step 21).
items.note: Checklist page N-8 · Training Manual page 22

items.title: ECS
items.text: Shown on BMS’s caution panel, but no BMS F-15C manual says what lights it. The ECS (work in progress in BMS) cools and pressurizes the cockpit and avionics with engine bleed air; the avionics switch to ram air when bleed air is off.
items.action: No procedure in the BMS F-15C checklist.

items.title: HOOK
items.text: The arresting hook is not up and locked. Not simulated in BMS: the Dash-1 marks this light N/I.
items.action: Arresting hook switch – UP unless you need the hook.

items.title: AUTO PLT
items.text: The Dash-1 does not say what lights it, only that pressing MASTER CAUTION resets it. The autopilot disengages itself beyond +4 g or below 0 g, with invalid INS attitude, or with a CAS axis off.
items.action: Reset MASTER CAUTION. To re-engage: attitude hold switch ON, then altitude hold ON; all three CAS axes must be engaged.

items.title: EQUIP HOT
items.text: Described by the Training Manual, but BMS’s caution panel picture shows no light with this legend. One cause it gives: more than 7–8 minutes below 8,000 ft with the gear down can shut the ECS off.
items.action: AIR SOURCE knob to normal (BOTH), throttles to 80% RPM. If it stays on: non-essential avionics off (the FCR shuts down by itself) and land at the earliest practical opportunity.

items.title: READY (JFS)
items.text: Green READY light on the engine control panel: the JFS is running and ready to be engaged to an engine. It goes out when the JFS shuts down after both engines are started.
items.action: Expect it within 10 s of pulling the JFS handle (15 s below 0°F). If the JFS will not engage, see JFS Fails to Engage; before another JFS start on a partly charged accumulator, service the JFS (ground comm menu T, 7).
items.note: Dash-1 pages 15, 66 · checklist pages N-5, EP-2

items.title: ALN
items.text: INS alignment light on the NCI: solid after about 60 s (coarse), flashing at 1 Hz after 120 s (partial), flashing at 4 Hz after 240 s (full alignment).
items.action: If it has not come on within about 60 s: check the ADI is erect, present position is displayed and the light tests good. To restart, NCI mode knob OFF for at least 2 s, then GC.

items.title: LEFT NOSE RIGHT
items.text: Green landing gear lights: all three on when the gear is down and locked; all out, with the gear handle light out, when it is up and locked.
items.action: A missing green with the gear handle light on is a gear malfunction: stay below 300 kt and see GEAR HANDLE under Warning lights.

items.title: FLAP
items.text: Flap position indicator: yellow while the flaps travel, green when they are down. Lowered flaps blow up above about 250 kt and come back down at about 240 kt.
items.action: Flaps DOWN for takeoff: check green (Before Taxiing step 11, Before Takeoff step 4).
items.note: Dash-1 pages 19, 51 · checklist pages N-7, N-9

items.title: READY (AR)
items.text: Air refueling READY light on the canopy bow: the air refueling (slipway) door is open.
items.action: Slipway switch – CLOSE when not refuelling; the Training Manual notes an open door costs nosewheel steering.

items.title: PROGRAM
items.text: Countermeasures dispenser in SEMI AUTO: a dispense program built from RWR threat data is ready.
items.action: Press the MAN 2 switch (left throttle) to dispense it. A MAN 1 or another MAN 2 command overrides it.

items.title: MINIMUM
items.text: Chaff or flare is down to the minimum quantity set in the data cartridge.
items.action: No procedure; the minimum is set through the data cartridge before flight.

items.title: CHAFF / FLARE
items.text: Blinking: that expendable is being dispensed. Steady: it is deselected with the DISP SEL switch on the CMD control panel.
items.action: Steady and you want it: DISP SEL switch to BOTH (or to that expendable).

items.text: BMS’s Voice Warning System is not yet fully implemented (Dash-1 4.1.2.1.66): the fire test plays a voice warning, but the manuals name no voice message other than OVER G. Its fixed-volume messages do not blank other audio and may not be heard.

items.title: OVER G, OVER G
items.text: Overload warning system: the aircraft has reached 100% of its maximum allowable g for the stores it carries. It repeats until the overload is relieved, and once started the full message (about 6 s) plays.
items.action: Reduce the g. The HUD shows current g and maximum allowable g.

items.title: OVER-G TONE
items.text: 900 Hz tone as the g nears the maximum allowable: beeping 4 times a second from 85%, 10 times a second from 92%, steady at 96–100%.
items.action: Ease the g before the voice warning at 100%. The HUD shows current and maximum allowable g.

items.title: DEPARTURE TONE
items.text: 900 Hz beeping tone warning of an impending departure: it starts at 30°/s yaw rate and beeps faster up to 60°/s.
items.note: Dash-1 page 21 (paragraph marked N/I) · Training Manual page 52

items.title: HIGH AOA TONE
items.text: High angle-of-attack warning tone: not implemented in BMS.

sections.title: JFS Fails to Engage or Abnormal Engagement/Disengagement

items.text: If no indication of light off 30 seconds after throttle is advanced to IDLE:
Engine Fails to Accelerate Normally (PW-220 Engine)
If both FTIT and RPM appear to stop increasing during start sequence:

If one of the following conditions occur during engine start, the starting FTIT limit of 680°C may be exceeded:
a. RPM acceleration simultaneous with or after after initial FTIT movement.
b. FTIT above 580°C with RPM below 40%.
c. FTIT rapidly rises thru 900°C.
d. RPM stops increasing then decreases while FTIT is stable or increases.

items.note: The JFS can be engaged when RPM below 30%.
The JFS can be engaged when RPM below 30%.

items.text: ALN Light Not On or Not Flashing (During Alignment)

If the ALN light does not illuminate within approximately 60 seconds, check that the ADI is erect (INS selected on the ADI mode switch), current present position (within 600ft/0.1 arc minutes) is displayed, and the ALN light tests good. If the ADI has not started to erect, the align cycle did not initialize. If the INS is shutdown (NCI mode selector knob in OFF), leave NCI mode selector knob in OFF for a minimum 2 seconds before initiating another alignment. Switching the NCI mode selector knob from NAV to GC or STOR causes the INS to start a new alignment cycle.
Aircraft Movement While in Align Mode

If the aircraft is moved while the INS is in an align mode, the INS auto-transitions to NAV mode and the ALN light stops flashing. After stopping the aircraft, the INU reenters the align mode and the ALN light begins flashing again after approximately 1 minute. As soon as the light begins flashing, the NCI mode selector knob may be placed in the NAV mode. If the alignment is not completed, the INS provides degraded navigational performance and should be restarted by turning the INS off (INS mode selector knob to OFF) for a minimum of 2 seconds, then to GC ALIGN for a full GC alignment. The NCI mode selector knob can then be switched to INS or the INS will automatically transition to Nav (INS) at aircraft takeoff.

Loss of normal brakes may be caused by a defective anti-skid system, faulty brakes, or a UTL A hydraulic pressure loss. Malfunction of the anti-skid system may not illuminate the anti-skid light; however, failures may be recognized by no apparent braking action. In any case, it is important to remember when assessing the status of brakes, that very little deceleration will be sensed by the pilot at speeds above 100 knots regardless of whether the anti-skid system has failed. Therefore, aerodynamic braking should be accomplished first during the landing roll, followed by braking action as required.
If brake failure occurs during landing roll, consider lowering the hook before attempting to restore braking.
If loss of the brakes is determined, turn the anti-skid switch to PULSER at high speed or OFF at taxi speed.
During pulser operation, pedal pressure over that required for safe deceleration may cause excessive tire wear and/or blown tires.

If braking is not restored, pulling the emergency brake/steering handle provides an alternate power source for brakes/steering and bypasses the anti-skid/pulser system. Sufficient accumulator pressure is available to safely stop the aircraft. Repeated brakes applications deplete the system faster than a smooth steady application. If UTL B is operating, the JFS accumulator remains charged. If the JFS LOW light is on, the emergency brake system is not reliable for taxi since the accumulator pressure can no longer be monitored. Do not pull the emergency brake/steering handle in flight as the nosewheel may follow rudder commands, and touchdown steering/wheel brake protection is lost. If UTL A is available, normal operation can be restored by pushing the emergency brake/steering handing and releasing the paddle switch. While taxiing, if stopping distance is critical, use the emergency brake/steering handle first.

Directional control problems with the nose gear on the ground may be caused by a blown tire, nose gear shimmy, defective nose gear steering, defective anti-skid, overextended strut, or a faulty brake. For a known blown tire or brake loss, refer to the appropriate emergency procedure. If the cause of the directional control problem cannot be determined, time spend in fault isolation may worsen the situation. In this case, a single procedure (pulling the emergency brake/steering handle) is recommended. This provides an alternate source for powered braking/steering and disables the anti-skid and pulser system(s), thereby accommodating all of the various failure modes which may have caused the directional control problems. NORMAL/MANEUVERING range steering continues to be available with the emergency brake/steering handle pulled.

If departure from a prepared runway, taxiway or ramp is unavoidable, consider shutting down the engines (time and conditions permitting) to minimize foreign object damage. Directional control while skidding or sliding across an unprepared surface may be impossible. If the aircraft develops a sideways skid or slide, failure of the landing gear is probable due to high side load forces. At higher speeds, aircraft roll, tumble, or groundloop is a possibility and consideration should be given to ground ejection if the situation warrants. Ground egress should not be attempted until the aircraft has come to a stop.

items.note: Because the anti-skid has been disabled, be prepared for a possible wheel lockup and a subsequent blown tire(s).
This ensures that the nose gear steering shifts to JFS hydraulic accumulator pressure.

items.text:
The decision to abort or continue the takeoff depends on many factors, most of which relate to a specific takeoff situation. Considerations should include, but are not limited to, the following:
a. Runway factors: Runway remaining, surface condition (wet, dry, etc.), type and/or number of arresting gear available, obstructions alongside or at the departure end, wind direction and velocity, weather and visibility.
b. Aircraft factors: Weight, stores configuration, nature of the emergency, velocity at decision point, and importance of getting airborne.
c. Stopping factors: Maximum braking, speed brake, hook, jettisoning stores, engine shutdown.
d. Full aft stick: Full aft stick will reduce stopping distance below computed TOLD data (up to 500 feet at max abort speed) by increasing drag and weight on wheels. However, full aft stick must be applied below rotation speed to avoid raising the nose.

Consider aborting after airborne where sufficient runway is available. Normally, with the short takeoff distances of the aircraft, abort is not a problem, but an early decision provides the most favorable circumstances.

items.note: If aborting with a blown tire or if a main tire blows during abort, place the anti-skid switch in PULSER, and use light braking on the good tire.

items.text: After an abort where unusual braking is required, do not shut down engines until adequate firefighting equipment is available. Hot wheels and brakes can provide an ignition source for fuel drained overboard during engine shutdown.
Two means exist to jettison external stores: the emergency jettison button, on the center instrument panel, and the select jettison button, on the ACP.
The emergency jettison button simultaneously jettisons all pylons and fuselage/CFT mounted missiles (N/I).
Do not use emergency jettison on the ground, or with fuseslage/CFT mounted missiles aboard, except as a last resort or in extreme emergency.

sections.title: Engine Failure/Loss of Thrust/Afterburner Failure on Takeoff

items.text: Do Depending on the type of failure and aircraft conditions, MIL power may not be sufficient to continue takeoff or sustain flight at low airspeed. If takeoff is continued use maximum power available in a three point attitude and accelerate to single engine takeoff speed. Once single engine rotation speed is attained, input 1/2 aft stick, and rotate to a 10° attitude. Reducing pitch (if able) and selecting maximum afterburner will allow the aircraft to accelerate.

If engine failure occurs after rotation, it may be necessary to lower the nose to the runway to attain single engine rotation speed. This is especially important at high gross weights and low-density altitudes. If an engine fails immediately after becoming airborne, it may be necessary to allow the aircraft to settle back to the runway until single engine rotation speed is attained. Immediately after becoming airborne, establish near level flight for acceleration prior to climb. Lateral and directional control can be maintained if the aircraft remains above stall speed, but the ability to climb depends upon the aircraft gross weight, configuration, airspeed, altitude and temperature.
Following an AB anomaly on takeoff and TOLD data requires afterburner, consideration should be given to aborting if conditions warrant.

items.action: lower to three-point attitude and accelerate to SETOS

items.text: With an engine failure or significant loss of thrust, if SETOS is not obtained by lowering nose to the runway, sustained flight may not be possible.
Delaying rotation until higher speeds improves single engine climb performance. Consider runway remaining and tire speed limits (nose 200, mains 225).

items.action: retract as soon as practical after takeoff

items.text: Gear retraction increases single engine rate of climb by 300-500FPM.
Accelerate and climb to a safe altitude and investigate
